pending_interview.category: System design (ML/AI-specific) — RAG at scale, eval pipeline design, recommendation systems, agent platforms, feature store design
pending_interview.question: You're designing a feature store for a large e-commerce company. A "feature store" is a centralized system that computes, stores, and serves the input signals (called "features") that machine learning models need to make predictions — for example, "how many times has this user clicked on a product in the last 7 days." The company has dozens of ML models in production, including a real-time product recommendation model that needs features with under 10 milliseconds of latency, and a weekly batch fraud-scoring model that processes hundreds of millions of transactions. Walk through how you would design this feature store to serve both use cases. How do you handle the fact that the same feature (say, "user purchase count in the last 30 days") might be needed in real time by one model and in batch by another? What does your storage layer look like, how do you avoid "training-serving skew" (where the data a model trained on differs from the data it sees in production), and what tradeoffs does your design introduce?
